channel.title: Engineering Digest
channel.description: Daily digest of engineering blog posts from top tech companies

item.title: Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Tunix and Gemma 4 on Google TPUs
item.description: This post walks developers through training a multi-turn, tool-using LLM agent using Tunix and Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs By leveraging agentic Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and asynchronous vLLM rollouts, the approach significantly improves complex reasoning and tool compliance in interactive environments.

item.title: The best things in open source are built together
item.description: Introducing Replica and the Open Source Accessibility Framework, new open source projects for collaboration and inclusion The post The best things in open source are built together appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

item.title: Internet traffic and attacks during the 2026 U.S. midterm elections
item.description: On November 3, 2026 U.S. voters headed to the polls Here’s what Cloudflare data across more than 1,400 protected sites tells us about Election Day Internet traffic and cyberattacks.

item.title: When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone?
item.description: TL;DR Teams building AI features want to skip slow A/B tests and decide from offline evals alone The post When Can You Ship on Offline Evals Alone? appeared first on Spotify Engineering.

item.title: An updated Clairic and Clairic-flash are now open-weight, from the new Workers AI Superintelligence team
item.description: Clairic graduates from preview, while Clairic-flash joins the repertoire on Workers AI We’re doing an open-weight release for both extraction models.

item.title: Building secure mobile apps in the agentic era
item.description: How we scale our security with attack surface maps, focused AI reviews, and checks that improve with every vulnerability fixed.

item.title: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances for Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances
item.description: AWS Lambda now supports GPU instances (G-series) for Event Functions running on Lambda Managed Instances, enabling serverless GPU workloads like machine learning inference, media processing, and rendering Lambda handles all infrastructure tasks, including instance lifecycle, driver management, and auto scaling, while maximizing GPU utilization across concurrent requests with standard EC2 pricing plus a management fee

item.title: How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models
item.description: Our previous post in this series introduced the Ranking Engineer Agent (REA), an autonomous system that generates hypotheses, designs experiments, and proves new machine learning (ML) techniques on ads ranking models Now, we’re sharing how we propagate ranking model improvements like architectural advancements and training optimizations efficiently across a large and diverse fleet of ads [...] Read More The post How Meta Uses AI Agents to Scale ML Innovations Across Ads Ranking Models appeared first on Engineering at Meta.

item.title: Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem
item.description: As ML ecosystems grow to a large number of production models, the bottleneck is no longer inventing new techniques to improve these models, but rather shipping them reliably and efficiently across a fragmented model space, creating a rising tide that lifts all the boats At Meta, we built a template-driven approach that standardizes model design [...] Read More The post Design Once, Deploy at Scale: Building a Template-Driven ML Ecosystem appeared first on Engineering at Meta.
